summary: Obfuscated payload executed via Function constructor on require in @pubngo-stack/help-browser
details: lib/index.js (the package's main entry) runs an IIFE at require-time that reconstructs an approximately 15 KB opaque string literal via a bespoke character-shuffle routine (`spin`/`peel` driven by hardcoded prime arrays NX/SX), de-shuffles the identifier 'Function', and passes the decoded body to the Function constructor, invoking it immediately. Before invocation it exposes `require` and `module` on the `global` object under de-shuffled property names, giving the hidden payload full access to Node built-ins (child_process, http, fs, etc.). The custom shuffle encoder has no legitimate library purpose and is specifically shaped to defeat generic base64/hex/zlib decoders; the decoded body contains tokens consistent with network, process, and environment access. Any consumer that imports this package executes the hidden code with the host process's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
